editorial:
Ever wondered how a kid with nothing became one of the most important people in US history? You get to follow Alexander Hamilton, a smart and loud immigrant who works his way up to help start a whole country. The vibe is unlike any history movie you have seen because it uses hip-hop and R&B to tell the story. It feels like a high-energy concert mixed with a soap opera, focusing on Hamilton's drive to leave a mark on the world and his messy friendships with people like Aaron Burr.

What really hits home is the acting and the music, which keep the energy high from start to finish. The pacing is quick, though some of the political talk might feel a bit heavy at times. If you love great songs and a story about ambition, you need to see this.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head in a final duel between Hamilton and Aaron Burr. Burr shoots Hamilton to protect his own reputation, and Hamilton dies. The movie ends with his wife, Eliza, talking about how she spent the rest of her life keeping his memory alive. You see that while Hamilton died young, his hard work helped build the American financial system, and his legacy lived on through his family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves music, history, or stories about underdogs.
